d: Their friend has been murdered, so cowboys "Lightning" Bill Carson (Tim McCoy) and Magpie McGillicuddy (Ben Corbett) are out for justice, leading Bill to don a mask and pose as "the Phantom.".
A frontier lawman partners with an American Indian detective to hunt down a ruthless band of teenage criminals known as the Rufus Buck Gang.
A retired Union contract scout embarks on a deadly mission to find out what happened to his true love and her little girl.
A blacksmith's daughter helps two lawmen round up a group of cattle rustlers.
A gang hijacks shipments of gold from Goldville. Ace Benton, the town's leading citizen is trying to acquire all the town property, as he knows the railroad is planning a line through there.
Hopalong Cassidy (William Boyd) and his sidekicks (George Hayes, Russell Hayden) stop rustlers and help a schoolmarm tame singing boys.
Their friend has been murdered, so cowboys "Lightning" Bill Carson (Tim McCoy) and Magpie McGillicuddy (Ben Corbett) are out for justice, leading Bill to don a mask and pose as "the Phantom.".
Maud Hoad leads her revenge-seeking family against Joe, who was forced to shoot treacherous Jeb Hoad.
Little Joe and Hoss are mistaken for gunmen while in a small Texas town; they find themselves in the middle of a dangerous feud between two families.
A corrupt Indian agent frames a Cherokee chief for horse theft.
Bandits seek a map revealing hidden treasure in a mission.
Range Rider (Jock Mahoney) tracks two kidnappers whose plans he and Dick (Dick Jones) interrupted. With Lonnie Burr, Pamela Blake.
An outlaw poses as the sheriff he murdered.
A killer's reign of terror keeps townspeople in their homes.
Range Rider (Jock Mahoney) and Dick (Dick Jones) capture a gang with the help of a U.S. marshal (Stanley Andrews) who was being held hostage.
Range Rider and Dick help when a respected rancher collapses in the street and the town doctor is held captive by outlaws.
Range Rider (Jock Mahoney) and Dick (Dick Jones) assist Jean Snyder (Pamela Blake) in building a telegraph line.

Sheriff Lawson wires for a Federal Land Commissioner to check on the various titles to land in the Mesquite district; One-Eye, under orders from Drake, attempts to halt the stagecoach and kill Treadway, the land agent.

st: Murder on the Santa Fe Trail
d: Mesquite banker Calvin Drake plans to profit from Santa Fe Railroad by gaining control of all the land in the territory.
Red carries Beth to shore after the stagecoach hits the water; Red and Beth capture Shark and bring him to the Mesquite jail.
Cherokee saves Red from certain death; Drake convinces the ranchers that the raids are over.
Red derails a mining car before it can crush him; the henchmen escape with the rancher's money.
Red escapes from the water tank hazard and orders the cowhands to start moving the cattle to the Lazy-W Ranch; Hanlon learns of this plan and prepares to stop them.
Red, carrying Beth, reaches the safety of an overhanging ledge; Red moves the herd to the BAR-M Ranch; to raise money, Red organizes a Wells-Fargo stagecoach race.
Dale unknowingly buys a stove containing stolen payroll money from a local peddler (Dub Taylor).
An attractive milliner and her grandfather are suspects in a plot to rob the Wells Fargo office.
Pat and his cousin inherit some land that is coveted by some unscrupulous ranchers.
Roy saves a group of archeological students taken hostage by robbers.
An outlaw gang tries to steal an old prospector's life savings.
An outlaw gang assigns an orphaned teenager (Harry Harvey, Jr.) the task of murdering Roy.
Roy debunks an old Western legend about a one-armed ghost.
A government agent is killed after he orders a stop to beaver trapping in the region.
A 10-year-old orphan (B.G. Norman) protects his uncle's illegal gold mine.
A lady banker turns to murder in order to gain possession of some oil-rich property.
A Colonial rebel (John Wayne) fights Indians, a British captain (George Sanders), and a seller of guns and liquor in Pennsylvania.
Three imprisoned soldiers agree to recover a cache of stolen Army gold in exchange for their freedom.
A crippled gunslinger trains an ex-convict to shoot, and together they ride out for revenge on the man who wronged them both.
An unlucky thief makes a friend in prison and from there goes hunting for buried gold.
Outlaw Belle Starr (Elsa Martinelli) foils the plans of a robber by beating him to the loot.
An outlaw and her four sisters fight an outlaw and her four brothers for oil in the 1880s New Mexico.
A potential mayoral candidate attempts to stir up trouble between majority and minority groups in town.
A former dance hall girl poses as a Spanish heiress to claim a land grant that includes part of the Ponderosa; guest Sebastian Cabot.

Silky saves the life of Bradshaw, a wounded Pinkerton detective. Together, they reach the cabin of Larry, and his sister Judy. Snowbound by a blizzard, an outlaw-killer and his gang arrive, and conflicts arise that bring dramatic & dangerous fights.
A prospecting party started out to find gold, but death makes a strike and the only survivors report they were poisoned with spoiled meat.
Silky finds himself in the awkward position of being a mail-order bridegroom when he stands in for the rich, girl-shy Cass, but the bride turns out to be a two-timer on a Yukon River boat adventure.

Silky finds himself sharing a jail cell with two miners, one of whom must be guilty of the murder of Nik Stavrous. With the help of Pierre and Marie, Silky upsets everybody's theory, including his own, about the identity of the gold-hungry killer.
Jaimie befriends a girl (Diana Millay) held as a servant by the leader of a group of buffalo skinners.

st: The Day of the Taboo Man
d: Doc and Jaimie risk an Indian attack to save a tribal outcast left to die in the wilderness.
The Matlock brothers challenge Buck for leadership of the caravan.
An Illinois widow (Olivia de Havilland) helps a Southern widower (Alan Ladd) traveling with his dog and mute son after the Civil War.
Adam and Little Joe warn Hoss when he tries to help Arnie, a man with the mind of a child and an uncontrollable temper.
An Easterner swears revenge for the death of his father, a drunk that a Cartwright killed in self-defense.
Hoss falls prey to a beautiful woman with a gambling addiction and refuses to believe she's only interested in his money.
Maud Hoad leads her revenge-seeking family against Joe, who was forced to shoot treacherous Jeb Hoad.
Little Joe and Hoss are mistaken for gunmen while in a small Texas town; they find themselves in the middle of a dangerous feud between two families.
A potential mayoral candidate attempts to stir up trouble between majority and minority groups in town.
A sadistic Chicago lawman comes to 1931 Virginia to shut down the Bondurant brothers' bootlegging business.
An old trapper (Richard Boone) helps a young man (Stewart Petersen) find his sister, abducted by Indians.
U.S. marshals (Johnny Mack Brown, Raymond Hatton) stop stagecoach robbers with help from one of the robbers (Marshall Reed).
A cheated prospector (John Wayne) and a crooked gold official (Randolph Scott) have an epic brawl over a Yukon saloon queen (Marlene Dietrich).
Agent Saunders (John Wayne) becomes partners with Fay (Cecelia Parker) to help her fight off a gang run by a local land grabber.
Jeb Drummond is a murderous sheep herder who has Adam taken hostage to try and force Ben to sign over a large section of Ponderosa land to him.
A Ponderosa ranch hand faces charges of killing the wife of the U.S. marshal who came to arrest him.
Two children of a kidnapped fur trapper are left alone in their cabin.
Roy and Dale question the identity of a man claiming to be a friend of the local minister.
A mysterious outlaw hijacks stolen loot from stagecoach bandits.
Roy exposes a fraudulent life insurance company.
When students become lawmen for a day, the new "sheriff's" uncle takes advantage.
A new family in Paradise Valley mistakes outlaws for a welcoming committee.
Outlaws misinterpret a comment made by Roy and Dale.
Gang of crooks locks Roy in his own jail. (1951).
Pat and Nellybelle are kidnapped by a gang of outlaws.
A teacher becomes increasingly nervous after a stagecoach robbery.
A young man decides to escape his overbearing father by joining the Carlson gang.
A trigger-happy rancher (Don C. Harvey) joins a posse searching for his brother-in-law.
While visiting a nearby town, Ray and Dale meet a girl (Frances Karath) whose horse was stolen.
Roy and Dale assist a young couple who are trying to reclaim their ranch.

Four escaped convicts descend on Mineral City looking for a former partner; Roy and most able-bodied men are hunting the desperadoes; the bad guys kidnap Dale, forcing her to show them where their partner now lives.
The town scavenger stumbles across counterfeit money left by outlaws.
Whit finally expresses his true feelings towards Grace; Lenny Hollister and Sanchez send the Champions an unusual gift.
After spotting stashed drugs on The Yellow Rose Ranch, an anticipated pursuit follows.
A cowboy (Johnny Mack Brown) and his partner (Raymond Hatton) ride where the lawless try to hide.
A free and peaceful town is saved from outlaws by a group of cowboys.
A man is falsely imprisoned on a murder charge, then escapes to join an outlaw gang and unmask the real killer.
A cowboy escorts a young half-Native American girl, whose mother has recently died. He must find her white father in order to claim her hefty inheritance.
When the showboat hits town, two men use the parade as a distraction to rob the bank.
When the showboat hits town, two men use the parade as a distraction to rob the bank.
Quick thinking saves Jim and Tombstone, but they have to return to Panamint for more money to repair the damage.
Tom Brandon, a young doctor who, working with and for the police department, takes a job as the doctor for a gang of criminals.
A football player is kidnapped by gangsters.
When the showboat hits town, two men use the parade as a distraction to rob the bank; their accomplice is Pop, the clown from the showboat.
A U.S. oil company field boss (Lew Ayres) kills a robbery suspect, then marries his widow (Teresa Wright) and flees to Mexico.
A cowboy (Johnny Mack Brown) and his partner (Raymond Hatton) ride where the lawless try to hide.
A free and peaceful town is saved from outlaws by a group of cowboys.
A man is falsely imprisoned on a murder charge, then escapes to join an outlaw gang and unmask the real killer.
As Ben prepares to run for governor, Joe must come to his rescue when a disabled police officer from New Orleans comes to arrest Ben on a 20-year-old murder charge.
Adam is taken hostage by a band of U.S. Army prisoners who have escaped and sought refuge on the Ponderosa.
Gordon rescues Amos Gray from the burning house and sends him home in Wilson's buckboard; Mulford's cattle are rated again; Mulford sends Radigan for the sheriff.
As Gordon crosses the river, the rustlers open fire and sink from sight; coming up behind dense brush, he hears them refer to Radigan as their leader.
Wealthy rancher John Mulford, unaware his foreman is a rustler, hires Buck Gordon; Gordon's search brings him to Ghost City.
Gordon rescues the girl, Mary Gray; he brings her back to Ghost City; the mystery man watches menacingly as they read his threatening note, then vanishes.
Mary goes with Gordon to Ghost City to show him her grandfather's gold mine; Gordon is left bound in a tunnel.
While inspecting the mine of Mary's Grandfather, Buck Gordon and Mary Gray narrowly escape an explosion; realizing someone was secretly working the mine, Mary returns home.
The bandits drag Buck with them; he gets away on Silver; the captured outlaws try to escape from the sheriff and one of them is shot.
Buck shoots the gun from his assailant's hand after dropping to the floor to dodge the bullets; next day Buck learns a railroad man is coming to town.
Buck is cornered by renegades in the cave; Silver lashes out with his heels and Buck rides away, chased by outlaws.
Buck leaps to his saddle and dashes away; Blake is badly injured, and Mary's papers are gone; The Phantom later sends her a note saying they are safe.
Cowboys rescue Mary and Buck; rustlers steal all Mary's cattle, her only source of money, when she has to meet a note at the bank.
A fight breaks out between settlers and natives over their shooting ability; Buck bursts from the closet carrying Mary and rushes her to their horses.
After Jeb Hollister undermines the Champions potential transaction for trucks to haul their cattle, they must find another way to get the job done.
Quisto Champion meets with Jeb Hollister to make a peace agreement; Juliette Hollister shows up to cover the cattle drive.
Two lawmen uncover a plot to steal a gold claim when they ride into town to investigate several killings.
Two-fisted cowboys fight for law and order in their encounters with outlaws.
Marshal John Carruthers helps a sheriff find out who stole the town's payroll, and together they discover the town's leader stole the money to buy up all the land.
A cowboy (John Wayne) protects a girl (Sheila Terry) and her father (George Hayes) from a rustler and a sheriff.
A U.S. Cavalry officer (Audie Murphy) falls in love with a part-Indian missionary (Linda Lawson) in Arizona.
